english.title: Person in respect of whom debt relief order made fail to comply with section 251J(5) duty
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a person in respect of whom a debt relief order was made as a result of an application, intentionally failed to comply with a duty to notify the official receiver as soon as reasonably practicable when

(A)_[there was an increase in your income during the moratorium period applicable to the order]_
(B)_[you acquired property during the moratorium period applicable to the order]_
(C)_[property was devolved upon you during the moratorium period applicable to the order]_
(D)_[when you became aware of an error in information supplied by you to the official receiver after the determination date]_
(E)_[when you became aware of an omission from information supplied by you to the official receiver after the determination date]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 251O(4)(a) of, and Schedule 10 to, the Insolvency Act 1986.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
debt relief order made as result of application
intentionally fail to comply with duty to notify official receiver
when increase in income / acquisition of property / property devolved during moratorium period applicable to order
OR became aware of error / omission from info supplied by official receiver after determination date

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

other.penalty:
Summary: Twelve months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
